Step 1:

#### Run Setup ####
    chmod +x setup.sh 
    ./setup

#### Verify IAM role attachment ####
    aws sts get-caller-identity


Step 2:

#### Change Directory ####
    cd ~/MemOpsAgent

#### Project Generation ####
    agentcore create

Step 3:

#### Move into the automatically generated directory using ####
    cd ~/MemOpsAgent/myMemOpsAgentProj

#### Open and adjust your regional environment targets map using ####
    nano agentcore/aws-targets.json 

#### Open the agent definition file located in the application directory ####
	nano app/myMemOpsAgentHar/harness.json


Step 4:

#### Clear any local build database artifacts to ensure a clean sync run using ####
	rm -rf .cli/rm -rf cdk.out/rm -f agentcore/.agentcore

#### Execute the native deployment command directly from the project directory using ####
	agentcore deploy


Step 5:

#### Test Agent ####

Code Interpreter — shows sandboxed Python execution:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Generate a Fibonacci sequence up to 100 and plot it as a bar chart"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Calculate the standard deviation of [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]"


Browser — shows web automation:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Go to https://aws.amazon.com and tell me the main headline on the page"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Search for the current AWS re:Invent date on the web and summarize what you find"

************************************** Scenario A — Short-Term Memory Validation *********************************
Run these two prompts in sequence without resetting your session:
   
   agentcore invoke --prompt "My production cluster has 3 nodes. Each node handles 450 requests per second at peak load."
   
Wait for a 30 to 90 seconds for the short term memory to get updated

   agentcore invoke --prompt "Based on what I just told you, what is the total peak request throughput across the entire cluster?"

NOTE : IT MIGHT TAKE TIME TO REGISTER IN THE SHORT TERM MEMORY SO EXECUTE THE SECOND PROMPT AFTER 30 SECONDS. IF YOU STILL GET A VALID RESPONSE THEN WAIT AND REEXECUTE THE PROMPT.
What to observe: The agent recalls the node count and per-node throughput from the first turn and uses it to answer the second question correctly, without you repeating the context. This confirms short-term memory is retaining up to 10 turns within the active session.


************************************** Scenario B — Long-Term Memory Validation **************************************
Run the first prompt, then close and reopen your terminal session, then run the second prompt:

    First Prompt : agentcore invoke --prompt "Remember this for future sessions: our critical incident threshold is 500ms response time and our on-call team lead is Alex."

Close your terminal, open a new session, then run: 

    Second Prompt : agentcore invoke --prompt "What is our critical incident threshold and who is our on-call team lead?"

What to observe: The agent retrieves the stored context from the previous session without being told again. This confirms long-term memory is persisting context across sessions within the 1 hour TTL window.

Step 6:

#### Remove All Resources ####

agentcore remove all

This single command tears down everything that was provisioned during deployment.

Confirm Removal
Once the command completes, confirm everything was torn down successfully:

agentcore list
